title: "Get started"
output: rmarkdown::html_document

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This guide introduces results, seats, preference votes and re-elections.
Install the stable package release and its canonical-data reader:

```{r installation}
install.packages(c("remotes", "nanoparquet"))
remotes::install_github("richardohrvall/swelections", ref = "v0.4.1")
library(swelections)
```

These examples use published canonical data and need no local raw-data archive.
Files are downloaded when first needed. See [Coverage](coverage.html) for
availability and [Accessing the data](accessing-data.html) for source choices.

## Results and geographic levels

Read the final 2022 parliamentary result nationally or by voting district:

```{r results}
national <- results(year = 2022, election = "parliamentary", level = "national")
head(national)

districts <- results(year = 2022, election = "parliamentary", level = "district")
head(districts)
```

Choose one level for an analysis. Totals such as ballots cast can repeat across
party rows; do not sum those repeated totals or add different geographic levels
together. Use `detail = "full"` for additional source information.

## Seats

Get municipal seat allocations, then select Stockholm by municipality code:

```{r seats}
municipal_seats <- seats(year = 2022, election = "municipal", level = "municipality")
stockholm <- subset(municipal_seats, municipality_code == "0180")
stockholm[, c("municipality_name", "party_abbreviation", "seats")]
sum(stockholm$seats) # 101 allocated seats
```

`seats()` describes electoral allocation. Use `members_at()` to find who held a
mandate on a date during a supported mandate period.

## Preference votes

Examine national preference votes in the 2024 European Parliament election:

```{r preferences}
personal <- preference_votes(year = 2024, election = "european", level = "national")
personal <- personal[order(personal$preference_votes, decreasing = TRUE), ]
head(personal[, c("party_abbreviation", "candidate_number", "preference_votes")])
```

Candidate numbers identify source records and must not be used to link people
across elections. Names may be missing even when preference votes are reported.

## Re-elections

Discover separate re-election events without downloading results:

```{r events, eval=TRUE}
library(swelections)
election_events(election_kind = "re_election")
```

The Swedish equivalent is:

```{r swedish-events, eval=TRUE}
valtillfallen(valklass = "omval")
```

Then request Falun's 2019 re-election result:

```{r falun}
falun <- results(
  year = 2019,
  election = "municipal",
  election_kind = "re_election"
)
head(falun)
```

A re-election is a separate event within the original mandate period. It does
not start a new ordinary election series or mandate period. See
[Coverage](coverage.html#re-elections) for supported re-election functions.

## Sources and language

The default `source = "auto"` is recommended for most users. It chooses approved
canonical data first, otherwise a supported remote source; never a local raw
archive. Choose a source explicitly when you need a particular input. See
[Accessing the data](accessing-data.html#source-selection-in-r) for explicit
source choices.

English functions return English columns and technical categories. Use
`names = "sv"` where supported, or Swedish functions such as `valresultat()`,
`mandat()` and `personroster()`. Proper names are preserved. For event discovery,
use `valtillfallen()` as the Swedish counterpart to `election_events()`.

See [Reference](../reference/index.html) for arguments and output definitions.
